results.independentDerivation: f′=x²e^(ax)(3+ax); f=f′ iff x²e^(ax)[(1−a)x−3]=0. The exponential is positive and x=0 always works. If a≠1, x=3/(1−a) is a distinct nonzero solution; if a=1 there is only x=0.

results.independentDerivation: At every intersection tan α is defined, so cos α≠0 and sin α=cos² α>0. Gradients −sin α and sec² α multiply to −1. With s=sin α, s²+s−1=0; positivity (also −(1+√5)/2<−1) selects s=(√5−1)/2 and sec² α=1/s=(1+√5)/2. This holds at every intersection, not merely a principal solution.
results.difficultyReason: Use the intersection equation to connect two derivative gradients, then combine a trigonometric identity with a quadratic and choose the admissible root.
